name: Queries for Number of Palindromes
description: You've got a string s = s 1 s 2 ... s | s | of length | s | , consisting of lowercase English letters. There also are q queries, each query is described by two integers l i , r i (1 ≤ l i ≤ r i ≤ | s |) . The answer to the query is the number of substrings of string s [ l i ... r i ] , which are palindromes. String s [ l ... r ] = s l s l + 1 ... s r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ | s |) is a substring of string s = s 1 s 2 ... s | s | . String t is called a palindrome , if it reads the same from left to right and from right to left. Formally, if t = t 1 t 2 ... t | t | = t | t | t | t | - 1 ... t 1 .
input_specification: The first line contains string s (1 ≤ | s | ≤ 5000) . The second line contains a single integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 10 6 ) — the number of queries. Next q lines contain the queries. The i -th of these lines contains two space-separated integers l i , r i (1 ≤ l i ≤ r i ≤ | s |) — the description of the i -th query. It is guaranteed that the given string consists only of lowercase English letters.
output_specification: Print q integers — the answers to the queries. Print the answers in the order, in which the queries are given in the input. Separate the printed numbers by whitespaces.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
